account:
There is an unusually large community gathering planned for eighteen today, and several people have been preparing it without initially explaining much to me. The innkeeper has invited me and said local helpers are organising it, that I need no prepared remarks, and that an escort will meet me at my office beforehand. The secretary is aware of the arrangement and has reserved the time. I intend to keep my afternoon appointments and be at the office for the escort.

The preparations are substantial: lanterns have been placed in the town hall, and yesterday I personally saw the builder and innkeeper deposit bread in a hall table chest. My neighbour identified the builder as coordinating supplies and lighting, and reported seeing the innkeeper pay the baker. This morning the baker said the innkeeper had verified that all two hundred feast loaves arrived. This looks like an organised communal feast, not a shortage or an unexplained disappearance of market bread; the baker says the stall still has bread available.

I suspect the gathering may include a surprise, possibly involving me, because preparations have been somewhat guarded and an escort is being arranged. But I do not know whom or what it celebrates, and I should not present that suspicion as fact. I have just asked the baker directly about the occasion and organisers, without yet receiving an answer.

Meanwhile, townsfolk around the mill and bakery keep repeating vague reports of a bridge or port change, sometimes naming the baker, innkeeper, and neighbour as present. I have witnessed no such change and have no confirmation. The baker actually asked me whether there was a confirmed bridge or ferry change, suggesting the rumour may be circulating without anyone knowing its basis. I told the baker and neighbour that I have no confirmed change to report and that the rumour is not official news.

I attended the mill at ten for the scheduled grain inspection and asked to see the stocks and hear about shortages, but have not obtained an inspection or a responsible person's report. That business remains unresolved.
